item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As a mathy person (who's OK with a some technically-incoherent silliness), this has been one of my favorite SCPs. I think that using the █ character, or doing something close to that, might have been better than [REDACTED], mostly since it's less annoying to use all over the place.

Also, the purpose of the redaction is to avoid "provoking" the SCP, rather than to hide information from humans. While it's mildly fun to figure stuff like that out, it's probably more realistic (and more friendly to people casually browsing the site) if the purpose of those redactions was purposefully called out in the article. Nonetheless, this one's a real classic in that it introduces something weird, yet comprehensible enough to be interesting, and does so very briefly.

At this point, SCP-2323 is taken. But it might be good to update this with something. E.g. a note saying something like: "Containment has been successful for the past X years, and SCP-2323 is taken, blah blah blah, thus no change is scheduled at this time, but in an emergency we will consider a change. If the SCP remains in operation, number 12167 is reserved." (23*23*23=12167) SCP-12167 would be in Series XIII; that passes the buck well down the line.

item.title: Re: Number nine
item.content:encoded:
Hmm. Well, just off the top of my head, it could have something to do with the fact that $3^2 = 9$ and $2^3 = 8$. It could be that SCP-233 doesn't like reversing its digits like that, or it could simply be that 8 is the largest number one can express using basic math, using only the numbers 2 and 3 in that order.

Of course, I'm not the author, so I dunno. Either way, I'm giving it an upvote because the mere fact you asked the question made me think about interesting things that I wasn't expecting to go into as a result of an SCP article.

item.content:encoded:
I understand the reason for the massive amount of redaction, and part of me finds it kinda funny. But the exact same effect (in-universe at least) could be accomplished without any of the redaction at all. Just say something like "Due to SCP-233's anomalous properties, all instances of the numeral expressed as the result of Equation A-233 will be represented in this document with the symbol Φ." Then you add an addendum showing that Equation A-233 is a reasonably simple formula that equates to 9. Obviously that example I gave is really clunky and would have to be cleaned up, but this

Under no circumstances are Φmm ammunition, Class D personnel born in the Φth month of the year or on the Φth, 1Φth, or 2Φth of the month, or any Φ-sided object to be brought within the 23-meter safe zone. Personnel are cautioned to take special care at Φ minutes past the hour, especially Φ hours, as this is the time period during which the object is most active. For best results, the 23-meter safe zone should be cleared of all personnel during that time period.

seems a lot less ridiculous to me than redactions every two words, even as I admit that the wording of the article would need retooling and not just a simple search-and-replace.

Also, there's a reference to SCP-233 having "already shown its value to the Organization", which I assume refers to the Foundation. I think my real issue with this article is that it really shows its age.

-1
